title: Physics Materials & Joints
description: Add bounciness and friction with Physics Materials, and explore connecting objects with Joints.

slides.title: Physics Materials 🏀
slides.content:
# Surface Properties

A **Physics Material** defines how a collider's surface behaves during collisions. Create one: **Project window → Create → Physics Material**.

Properties:
- **Dynamic Friction** – friction when moving (0 = ice, 1 = rubber).
- **Static Friction** – friction to start moving.
- **Bounciness** – how much it bounces (0 = no bounce, 1 = perfect bounce).
- **Friction Combine** / **Bounce Combine** – how to combine with the other object's material (Average, Minimum, Multiply, Maximum).

Assign it to a Collider's **Material** slot.

quizData.question: What does Bounciness = 1 mean?
quizData.explanation: Bounciness 1 means perfectly elastic collisions; 0 means inelastic (no bounce).

slides.title: Friction & Bounce Combine Modes 🔗
slides.content:
# How Surfaces Mix

When two colliders meet, Unity uses their combine modes to calculate final properties:
- **Average** – (A+B)/2.
- **Minimum** – smaller of the two.
- **Multiply** – A × B.
- **Maximum** – larger of the two.

Default is Average, which gives a middle ground. For gameplay tweaks, you can override per object.

slides.title: Joints – Connecting Objects ⛓️
slides.content:
# Physical Connections

Joints allow you to physically link two GameObjects. Common joints:

- **Fixed Joint** – glues objects together.
- **Hinge Joint** – door, seesaw (rotates around one axis).
- **Spring Joint** – stretchy connection.
- **Configurable Joint** – do‑it‑all, very powerful.

All joints rely on Rigidbody components. You can set limits, motors, and break forces.

Example: a door with a Hinge Joint on one side.

quizData.question: Which joint would you use for a swinging door?
quizData.explanation: Hinge Joint allows rotation around a single axis, perfect for doors.

slides.title: Creating a Simple Bouncy Ball
slides.content: Set up a sphere with Rigidbody and a Physics Material with high bounciness.

slides.title: 2D Physics Materials 📄
slides.content:
# For 2D Games

There's also **Physics Material 2D** (Create → 2D → Physics Material 2D). Similar properties: Friction, Bounciness, but for 2D colliders.

Always use the correct version; 3D materials won't work on 2D colliders and vice versa.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Bouncy Objects? Add Continuous Detection

Fast bouncing objects can tunnel through floors. Set Rigidbody Collision Detection to Continuous Dynamic to prevent this.
